text:
Every year, many people leave their villages for big cities, while others do the reverse, and opinions differ on whether city life or countryside life is preferable. This essay will consider both views before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of city life argue that it offers opportunity and variety. Cities have jobs, universities and entertainment, and they provide excellent hospitals, shops and public transport. A young engineer, for example, will find many employers and professional contacts in a city, and she can attend concerts, exhibitions and sports events at weekends. Cities also bring together people of different cultures, which broadens the mind and makes life interesting. For people who value convenience, everything from food delivery to medical specialists is close at hand.

On the other hand, supporters of the countryside argue that it offers peace and community. Rural areas are quiet, affordable and close-knit but lack services and employment. A family that moves to a village, for example, may afford a house with a garden for the price of a small city flat, and children can play outdoors safely. Fresh air, open space and contact with nature improve health and reduce stress. Neighbours know and help each other, which builds a strong sense of belonging. However, the disadvantages include long journeys to hospitals and schools, limited choice of jobs and fewer cultural activities. Cities, in contrast, are expensive, noisy and polluted.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that the choice depends on stage of life and priorities: city life suits young people who are building careers, while the countryside suits families and retired people who value tranquillity.

Yên bình và cộng đồng: yên tĩnh, rẻ, gắn bó; ví dụ gia đình chuyển về làng mua nhà có vườn giá căn hộ nhỏ, trẻ chơi ngoài trời; không khí, thiên nhiên; hàng xóm giúp nhau; nhược: xa bệnh viện, ít việc, ít văn hoá; thành phố đắt, ồn, ô nhiễm.
